disposition_reason: Primary study reporting Cd and Pb (mg/kg fresh weight) by botanical honey type for 35 beekeeper honeys from eastern Morocco.

study.design: beekeeper sampling, composition survey by botanical origin
study.material_scope: Honey of seven botanical types: jujube, multifloral, citrus, eucalyptus, thyme, carob, rosemary
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Growing origin: eastern Morocco — Oujda (Angad), Berkane (Tafoughalt), Jerada (Guenfouda), Nador (Aroui), Taourirt (Naïma); obtained directly from beekeepers (not retail).
study.sampling_unit: honey samples (per-type n not stated in main text)
study.method: 0.5 g honey digested in 5 mL aqua regia (3.5 mL HCl + 1.5 mL HNO3) under reflux 2 h, filtered, made to 50 mL; Perkin Elmer AAS AAnalyst 800 (text also lists ICP-style plasma parameters — see unresolved)
study.qa: Triplicate analyses; no CRM, recovery, or blank data reported.

findings.censoring: No non-detects or LOD/LOQ reported; all values printed as quantified means.
findings.notes: Number of samples per honey type not stated in the main text (35 samples across 7 types; Table S1/S2 with per-type data not available in the primary file). Table 2 is described as 'mean ± standard deviation' and Section 3.4 says 'triplicate analyses for all measurements', so it is unclear whether SD is across samples or replicate analyses. Statistical letters are all 'a' for Cd and Pb (no significant difference among types). Origin: eastern Morocco beekeepers (Oujda-Angad, Berkane-Tafoughalt, Jerada-Guenfouda, Nador-Aroui, Taourirt-Naïma); per-type origin given only in unavailable Table S2. Reported SD (0.01) exceeds the mean (0.0019) — implausible for a non-negative quantity unless values span non-detects; not resolvable from the text.

controls.outcome: Authors cite (ref. 49) that honey contamination with heavy metals often stems from non-hygienic harvesting/processing; not tested in this study.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Title differs: primary is 'Unveiling the Mineral and Sugar Richness of Moroccan Honeys: A Study of Botanical Origins and Quality Indicators'; summary gives 'Mineral Profile and Heavy Metal Content of Seven Monofloral and Multifloral Honeys from Eastern Morocco'. DOI (10.3390/molecules30010150) matches.

Author list differs: primary = Abeslami, El Farissi, Cacciola, El Bachiri, Sindic, Fauconnier, Bruneau, Talhaoui; summary lists Oulad El Majdoub, Mondello, Alaiz, Vioque (not authors) and omits Sindic, Fauconnier, Bruneau, Talhaoui.
Method: summary says ICP-MS; primary says AAS (Perkin Elmer AAnalyst 800) after aqua-regia reflux digestion.
Honey types: summary lists thyme, jujube, carob, lavender, rosemary, euphorbia, multifloral; primary has jujube, multifloral, citrus, eucalyptus, thyme, carob, rosemary (no lavender or euphorbia).
Provinces: summary says Oujda-Angad and Driouch; primary lists Oujda (Angad), Berkane, Jerada, Nador, Taourirt (no Driouch).
Sample size: summary says per-variety n 'not clearly stated' and sample_n null; primary states 35 honey samples in total (Section 3.1; Figure 2).
Pb range: summary says 0.13–0.19 mg/kg; primary Table 2 and text give 0.09 (thyme) to 0.19 (multifloral) mg/kg; carob 0.10.
Cd range: summary says 0.0017–0.018 mg/kg; primary Table 2 and text give 0.0014 (thyme) to 0.018 (multifloral).
Summary claims melissopalynological confirmation of botanical origin; not described in the primary text.
Summary claims LOD/LOQ values were reported for each analyte and Cd/Pb above LOQ in all samples; primary reports no LOD/LOQ.
Summary frontmatter metals include Cr, Ni, Zn, Cu as heavy metals; primary did not measure Cr or Ni (measured K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, Cd, Pb).
Summary gives collection '2022–2023 (year estimated from publication)'; the primary reports no collection period (estimating from the publication year is not allowed).
Summary says total minerals for monofloral types ranged '~200 to ~550 mg/kg' and K '100–400 mg/kg'; Table 2 K ranges 49.31–452.66 mg/kg.

Summary's regulatory framing (EU recommended Pb 0.10 mg/kg, Recommendation 2014/663/EU) is not in the primary; the primary (p. 5) says Pb values 'exceeded the Codex Alimentarius and European Union standards, which set a limit at 0.3 mg/kg' — internally contradictory, since all values are below 0.3.
unresolved: Per-type sample counts are not in the main text (Table S1/S2 not in the primary file); n set to null for type means.
Instrument ambiguity: Section 3.3 names an AAS (AAnalyst 800) but lists ICP plasma parameters (RF power, argon plasma gas flow, viewing height), which do not apply to flame/furnace AAS.
Cd SDs exceed the means for all seven types (e.g., 0.0019 ± 0.01); cannot tell whether the SDs are misprinted or reflect censored or near-zero values.
Section 2.2 states Cd/Pb averages 'ranging from 0.00075 to 0.14 mg/kg', which does not match Table 2.
Regulatory sentence on p. 5 is self-contradictory (says Pb 'exceeded' a 0.3 mg/kg limit, but the maximum is 0.19).
PCA Table 3 lists 'Pd' (palladium) with loadings; Pd was not among the nine measured elements — most likely a typo for Pb, not confirmed.
Storage before analysis: sealed plastic container at 22–24 °C (Section 3.1) — noted as method context, not a tested control.
